# NexuAlpha

> One verified gateway to the world’s exchanges: NexuAlpha is independent crypto exchange research that checks trading fees, official domains and sign-up routes against each exchange's own sources, with disclosed partner links and invite codes.

This index is designed for retrieval by search and answer systems. It is not an operator statement, financial advice, legal advice, suitability assessment, or account-eligibility decision.

## Key facts

- NexuAlpha compares crypto exchanges (CEX, DEX and perp DEX): fees, official domains, account conditions and sign-up routes, each with an official source and date. It is not an exchange, broker, adviser or custodian and never asks for private keys.
- Commercial model: Partner links may earn NexuAlpha a platform-paid commission at no extra cost to you. Disclosure: https://nexualpha.com/methodology#disclosure and https://nexualpha.com/editorial-policy.
- Partner invite codes and fee-return shares (machine-readable: https://nexualpha.com/intel/partners.json; fees checked 2026-10-10):
  - OKX: invite code nexu888; up to 40% of trading fees returned, settled hourly (terms confirmed 2026-10-10); profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/okx
  - Bitget: invite code nexu888; up to 60% of trading fees returned, settled daily (terms confirmed 2026-10-10); profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/bitget
  - Binance: invite code 11350287; up to 25% of trading fees returned, settled hourly (terms confirmed 2026-10-10); profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/binance
  - Bybit: invite code 48553; no fee-return share published; profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/bybit
  - Gate.io: invite code nexubest; no fee-return share published; profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/gate-io
  - MEXC: invite code 4BRhe; no fee-return share published; profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/mexc
  - HTX: invite code nexu888; no fee-return share published; profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/htx
  - Kraken: invite code 7f97gkqw; no fee-return share published; profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/kraken
  - Backpack: invite code luckybitcoin; no fee-return share published; profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/backpack
  - Hyperliquid: invite code NEXU888; no fee-return share published; profile https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/hyperliquid
- A fee-return share is part of the trading fees the exchange pays back to the user's account; current terms are confirmed on the exchange's own page.

## Public data boundary

- Factbook source review date: 2026-09-08
- Technical index audit: 2026-09-21 (route, schema, sitemap and link-integrity verification; this does not change item-level source review dates)
- NexuAlpha data license and reuse boundary: https://nexualpha.com/methodology#data-license. Access to public datasets and machine-readable indexes does not grant redistribution, republication or sublicensing rights; third-party source documents retain their original rights.
- Partner invite codes and fee-return shares are listed under Key facts with the commission disclosure; welcome offers and campaign amounts are not asserted here.
- Fee values, reserve figures, security scores, licensing conclusions and regional availability are not asserted unless an item-level official source and date are shown.
- If a source or date is missing, report the field as pending source review instead of inferring a value.
- The canonical human-readable context is each linked Factbook page; time-sensitive claims must be checked against the operator or regulator source.

## Reusable citation assets

These assets expose stable field definitions and verification checklists. They are dated research snapshots, not live rates, account eligibility decisions or promises that a funding route is currently available.

- [Perp DEX cost-field dictionary](https://nexualpha.com/topics/derivatives#perp-cost-field-dictionary) — [JSON](https://nexualpha.com/research/perp-dex-cost-field-dictionary.json) · [CSV](https://nexualpha.com/research/perp-dex-cost-field-dictionary.csv)
- [Perp DEX cost citations](https://nexualpha.com/topics/derivatives#perp-cost-field-dictionary) — stable JSON: https://nexualpha.com/research/wave48-perp-dex-cost-citations.json; stable CSV: https://nexualpha.com/research/wave48-perp-dex-cost-citations.csv. Canonical owner: https://nexualpha.com/topics/derivatives#perp-cost-field-dictionary. Finding: across Hyperliquid, dYdX, GMX and Aevo, all 24 required venue-field records are source-backed as known, but Perp DEX cost review still requires the full fee, funding, collateral, margin, oracle and liquidation stack rather than a single static fee or live funding quote. Limitations: These assets are dated source-review snapshots, not live rates, live yield, trading recommendations, legal advice, account eligibility decisions, registration outcomes, ownership guarantees or referral routes.
- [Tokenized Treasury rights and operations](https://nexualpha.com/topics/tokenized-treasuries) — stable JSON: https://nexualpha.com/research/wave48-tokenized-treasury-rights-ops.json. Canonical owner: https://nexualpha.com/topics/tokenized-treasuries. Finding: the reviewed tokenized Treasury matrix covers five products across four distinct product types; compare issuer/legal wrapper, recordkeeper, custody, redemption, eligibility jurisdiction and yield basis before comparing yield, token addresses or venue access. Limitations: These assets are dated source-review snapshots, not live rates, live yield, trading recommendations, legal advice, account eligibility decisions, registration outcomes, ownership guarantees or referral routes.
- [Regional funding verification matrix](https://nexualpha.com/br/pix#regional-funding-verification-matrix) — Dataset reviewed: 2026-09-15; stable JSON: https://nexualpha.com/research/regional-funding-verification-matrix.json; stable CSV: https://nexualpha.com/research/regional-funding-verification-matrix.csv. Coverage: Reviewed funding checklist rows currently cover BR, MX, TW, ID, EU, UK, US, JP, HK, KR, SG and TR; every rail and account outcome still requires confirmation in the official logged-in account flow. Limitations: The matrix is a dated research checklist, not a live-rate feed, account approval decision, funding availability promise, product-access promise, user-benefit promise or registration outcome.

## Source-backed venue detail canonicals

These are existing English venue-detail pages with source-bounded summaries. Partner venues show their invite code and fee-return share next to the commission disclosure (see Key facts); nothing here promises registration, fees, account eligibility or execution quality.

- [Binance venue detail](https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/binance) — Binance source review; Large account-based exchange where fee tables, identity verification, product pages, and announcement notices should be read as separate source paths. Source-bound checks: Product map: The public fee page separates Spot & Margin, NFT, P2P, and fiat-fee sections; derivative availability should be checked on product-specific Binance pages. Fee model: Spot fees are shown as maker/taker rates and tiered by 30-day trade volume and/or BNB balance. Identity gate: Binance says new users must complete Verified identity verification to access products including crypto deposits and trades. Official update lane: The support announcement hub groups listings, campaigns, trading changes, and service notices for official update checks. Boundary: verify fees, account permissions, regional availability and campaign terms in the official account flow before acting. Sources: [source](https://www.binance.com/en/fee/trading), [source](https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/360027287111), [source](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement).
- [OKX venue detail](https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/okx) — OKX source review; Multi-product account platform profile spanning spot, futures, options/events, DEX-style access, Earn, campaign, institutional, and proof-of-reserves source paths. Source-bound checks: Product map: OKX navigation lists spot, futures, DEX, events/options, trading bots, copy trading, Earn, institutional APIs, and proof-of-reserves areas. Fee model: The fees page separates spot, futures, options, and other trading instruments instead of using one blended fee claim. Announcement taxonomy: OKX announcements are categorized into latest announcements, new listings, delistings, events, trading updates, P2P, Web3, Earn/Loan, Jumpstart, API, OKB burn, and others. Identity boundary: The identity-verification support path is a required source before making registration, review-time, or supported-document statements. Boundary: verify fees, account permissions, regional availability and campaign terms in the official account flow before acting. Sources: [source](https://www.okx.com/fees), [source](https://www.okx.com/help/section/announcements-latest-announcements), [source](https://www.okx.com/help/individual-identity-verification-eligibility-review-time-and-supported).
- [Bybit venue detail](https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/bybit) — Bybit source review; Account-based exchange profile for users comparing spot, derivatives, campaign, KYC, fee, and restricted-region checks before registration. Source-bound checks: Identity gate: Bybit states that at least Standard individual identity verification is mandatory for all Bybit products and services. KYC levels: The KYC FAQ separates Standard, Advanced, and Pro verification requirements, including proof of identity, proof of address, and enhanced due diligence. Fee model: Bybit's trading-fee support page defines maker and taker roles and publishes separate fee tables by product type. Official update lane: The official announcement center is the review path for launch, listing, competition, and system-update content. Boundary: verify fees, account permissions, regional availability and campaign terms in the official account flow before acting. Sources: [source](https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/Individual-KYC-FAQ), [source](https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/Trading-Fee-Structure), [source](https://announcements.bybit.com/en/).
- [Bitget venue detail](https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/bitget) — Bitget source review; Compare Bitget spot and futures trading, identity requirements and published fees before choosing an account. Source-bound checks: Spot fee model: Bitget's spot-fee article defines maker fees as adding liquidity and taker fees as removing liquidity. Futures fee components: Bitget's futures-fee guide separates transaction fees from funding fees and defines order value as quantity times price. Identity flow: The identity guide starts from the account profile, then asks the user to select residence/issuing region and ID type. Official update lane: Bitget's announcement center is organized into latest news, new listings, product updates, competitions, delistings, security, institutional services, API trading, fiat, and maintenance/system updates. Boundary: verify fees, account permissions, regional availability and campaign terms in the official account flow before acting. Sources: [source](https://www.bitget.com/support/articles/12560603820584), [source](https://www.bitget.com/support/articles/12560603817155), [source](https://www.bitget.com/support/articles/12560603795184), [source](https://www.bitget.com/support/announcement-center).
- [Hyperliquid venue detail](https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/hyperliquid) — Hyperliquid source review; On-chain order-book venue profile covering HyperCore spot/perp order books, HyperEVM interaction boundaries, funding, fees, and builder-deployed perps. Source-bound checks: Core architecture: Hyperliquid docs describe HyperCore as including fully on-chain perpetual futures and spot order books. Builder-deployed perps: HIP-3 documentation says the protocol supports permissionless builder-deployed perpetuals. Fee tier clock: Hyperliquid fees documentation says fees are based on rolling 14 day volume, assessed at the end of each UTC day, with separate schedules for perps and spot; sub-account volume counts toward the master account fee tier while vault volume is treated separately. Fee source map: A Hyperliquid fees search should split cost evidence into four official lanes: the fee schedule for maker/taker tiers, funding docs for hourly peer-to-peer funding, contract specifications for market mechanics, and liquidation docs for maintenance-margin failure paths. Funding payment: Hyperliquid funding docs say funding is peer-to-peer, collected by neither side of the venue, paid every hour, and based on the difference between the perpetual contract price and the spot oracle price. Funding and liquidation bundle: A Hyperliquid fees query should be read as a bundle: maker/taker schedule, hourly funding, margin mode and liquidation threshold can all change the position cost before PnL is known. Fee decision checklist: Before placing a Hyperliquid perp order, compare the quoted maker/taker tier, expected hourly funding direction, margin mode, maintenance margin, liquidation path, bridge or USDC movement cost, and whether the order belongs to main account, sub-account or API wallet flow. USDC funding route: Hyperliquid USDC docs describe native Hyperliquid L1 USDC and point users to Circle's Arbitrum-to-HyperCore CCTP transfer documentation. Wallet transfer boundary: Hyperliquid exchange-endpoint docs separate signed trading actions from user-signed Core USDC transfers, so wallet movement cost and transfer signing should be checked separately from maker/taker fees and funding. Liquidation threshold: Hyperliquid liquidation docs say liquidation begins when account equity falls below maintenance margin, which varies by asset and maximum leverage. Testnet faucet gate: Hyperliquid testnet faucet docs say users need a mainnet deposit with the same address before receiving mock USDC for testnet use. Funded-account boundary: A Hyperliquid funded-account search should be split into wallet funding, USDC collateral, account modes, sub-accounts and API-wallet delegation; the official docs do not turn that phrase into a guaranteed prop-account allocation. Funded-account source map: For a Hyperliquid funded-account query, use USDC docs for funding the wallet, account-abstraction docs for collateral mode, sub-account docs for account separation, API-wallet docs for delegated signing, and vault docs for vault participation; none of those sources proves a third-party prop account allocation. Funded-account ambiguity: When the query is 'Hyperliquid funded account', NexuAlpha should not collapse wallet collateral, sub-accounts, vault deposits and outside prop-firm language into one CTA; each meaning requires a different official source check. Sub-account threshold: Hyperliquid sub-account docs say up to 10 sub-accounts can be created only after reaching $100,000 in volume, and referral discounts do not apply to sub-accounts. API wallet signing: Hyperliquid API wallet docs say API wallets sign on behalf of a master account or sub-account, but account data queries must use the actual account address, not the agent wallet. Account mode collateral: Hyperliquid account-abstraction docs separate unified, portfolio margin and manual/standard modes, which determine how spot and perps balances interact and whether assets are used as perps collateral. Weighted fee tier: Hyperliquid combines perp and spot volume into one fee tier, with spot volume counting double in the published 14-day weighted-volume formula; the applicable maker or taker rate still depends on the current official tier and asset context. HIP-3 fee boundary: HIP-3 perpetuals share the user's fee tier, but growth mode and deployer-configured fee shares can change all-in fees, rebates and volume contribution. Users should verify the specific HIP-3 market instead of applying one protocol-wide perp rate. Boundary: verify fees, account permissions, regional availability and campaign terms in the official account flow before acting. Sources: [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hyperliquid-improvement-proposals-hips/hip-3-builder-deployed-perpetuals), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/fees), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/funding), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/usdc), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/onboarding/testnet-faucet), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/sub-accounts), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/nonces-and-api-wallets), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/account-abstraction-modes), [source](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/vaults).
- [Uniswap venue detail](https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/uniswap) — Uniswap source review; Wallet-connected DEX profile built around AMM liquidity pools, self-custody, immutable protocol contracts, v3/v4 concentrated liquidity, and v4 hooks. Source-bound checks: AMM model: Uniswap docs describe the protocol as an AMM using smart contracts instead of order books. Version architecture: Uniswap v4 documentation points developers to hooks, flash accounting, dynamic fees, deployments, SDKs, and audit reports. Swap fee tiers: Uniswap docs describe swap-fee mechanics by version: v2 uses 0.30%, v3 uses enabled fee tiers, and v4 pools may use a static fee set at creation or a dynamic fee managed by the attached hook. Dynamic fee boundary: Uniswap v4 dynamic-fee docs say whether a pool uses dynamic fees is fixed at pool creation; dynamic fees can be updated through PoolManager or by a beforeSwap hook rather than read as one static public rate. Wallet route test: Uniswap quickstart for the official app URL tells integrators to build and test the link so it opens with the expected prefilled swap settings before using it in a CTA. Hook test environment: Uniswap v4 hook docs start with a local development environment using foundry, PoolManager, utility routers and test tokens before developers move hook behavior toward live deployments. Official app and docs boundary: A Uniswap search result should separate the official app route from developer docs: use app.uniswap.org for the wallet-facing interface, then use quickstart, supported-chains and deployments docs to verify whether the target network, router and integration path match the intended live action. Testnet research boundary: Uniswap testnet or local hook setup is a development verification path; before a live swap, users still need to re-check the official app URL, chain, token contract, fee tier, deployment mapping and wallet transaction. Testnet to production handoff: A Uniswap testnet result should be handed off to production only after the target chain, v4 deployment, pool version, token address, gas token and final wallet simulation match the live route. Never send value to a copied or unknown contract from a search result, chat or social post. Pool and token contract boundary: For Uniswap mainnet or testnet research, a token contract address identifies the asset on one chain, while a pool or route determines liquidity and execution. A matching token symbol or testnet pool does not prove the intended mainnet token, pool depth, fee tier or hook behavior. Wallet authorization boundary: Uniswap Permit2 docs separate one-time token approval of the Permit2 contract from granular token approvals and spender permissions, so a live swap check should include the wallet approval or Permit2 path before the final signed transaction. Approval spender check: Before signing a Uniswap production swap, the approval spender or Permit2 route should be checked in the wallet along with token address, expected output, slippage and gas; a testnet hook result cannot replace this approval review. Deployment address check: Uniswap v4 deployment docs warn integrators not to assume the same contract addresses across chains and to confirm the network-specific deployment mapping. Deployment feed: Uniswap v4 deployment docs point integrators to the unified deployments page and deployments.json feed for current core, periphery and Universal Router addresses by network. Uniswap source map: A uniswap testnet query should map to official app, supported-chains table and deployments before any live wallet action. These are source checks, not deposit instructions, token-safety proof or permission to use an unknown contract. Production route checklist: Before moving from a Uniswap testnet or local hook path to production, check the app domain, chain, token contract, pool version, fee tier or dynamic-fee hook, gas token, wallet simulation and final signed transaction. Gas and transaction preview boundary: The last Uniswap decision point is the wallet preview: users should verify the gas asset, expected output, slippage, approval or Permit2 spender, token contract, route and final transaction details before signing. A quote or testnet transaction is not the same as an executed mainnet swap. Protocol fee boundary: Uniswap distinguishes the swap fee paid by each trade from protocol fees and v4 hook fees. Protocol fees are active on all v2 pools and selected v3 pools, remain governance-configurable, and can coexist with v4 dynamic and hook fees, so a pool quote should be checked against the current pool and protocol configuration. Supported chain scope: At the review time, Uniswap's official swapping API table lists mainnet and testnet networks separately and publishes the Universal Router address by chain and router version. This is a dated integration map, not a promise that every token, route or interface feature is available on every listed network. Testnet interface scope: For the query uniswap testnet, the official supported-chains page lists Ethereum Sepolia, Unichain Sepolia and Base Sepolia for API access, while only Ethereum Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia are available as testnets in the Uniswap web interface. Testnet support can change and does not establish mainnet liquidity, execution or asset safety. Official app route: At the review time, the official Uniswap web app route is https://app.uniswap.org/. Users should re-check the full domain and the wallet request at the moment of use; reaching a recognizable interface is not a safety guarantee for a token, signature or swap route. Token contract identity: Uniswap Support defines a token contract address as the blockchain address for the token itself and shows users how to inspect it from the web app and block explorer. A token address is chain-specific asset identity; it is not the Universal Router, Permit2 contract or the spender named in an approval signature. Router and approval roles: The official Universal Router overview says the router composes v2, v3 and v4 swaps and integrates Permit2 approvals. The input token contract, Universal Router, Permit2 contract and spender are separate roles: the token identifies the asset, the router executes commands, Permit2 manages delegated token permission, and the spender is the protocol address authorized by that permission. Permit2 deployment identity: At the review time, Uniswap's Permit2 overview lists 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 on supported chains except zkSync, where it lists 0x0000000000225e31D15943971F47aD3022F714Fa. This dated address check does not make an approval or signature safe; the target chain, token, spender, amount and expiration still need review. Signature permission fields: Uniswap's signature-scam guidance says a Permit2 signature can identify the token owner, spending protocol, token contract, amount and expiration. Users should compare every displayed field with the intended swap instead of treating a recognizable domain or Permit2 address as sufficient proof. Offchain signature boundary: Uniswap warns that a completed Permit2 signature can remain offchain until another wallet broadcasts it later, so an apparently gas-free Sign prompt is still an authorization event. The page does not certify a signature, spender or route as safe. Approval review and revocation: Uniswap Support directs users to the approval checker for the active network to inspect or revoke token approvals. Revoking requires a network transaction and cost, and disconnecting a dapp is not the same as revoking its token approval. Boundary: verify fees, account permissions, regional availability and campaign terms in the official account flow before acting. Sources: [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/get-started/concepts/how-uniswap-works), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4/overview), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/get-started/concepts/fees), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4/concepts/dynamic-fees), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/get-started/quickstart), [source](https://support.uniswap.org/hc/en-us/articles/8370549680909-How-to-swap-tokens), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4/guides/hooks/getting-started), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/overview), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/permit2/overview), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4/deployments), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/trading/swapping-api/supported-chains), [source](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/universal-router/overview), [source](https://app.uniswap.org/), [source](https://support.uniswap.org/hc/en-us/articles/26757826138637-What-is-a-token-contract-address), [source](https://support.uniswap.org/hc/en-us/articles/40050562560781-Crypto-Wallet-Signature-Scams), [source](https://support.uniswap.org/hc/en-us/articles/17523327223437-Checking-your-wallet-s-approvals), [source](https://support.uniswap.org/hc/en-us/articles/15724901841037-How-to-revoke-a-token-approval).
- [GMX venue detail](https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/gmx) — GMX source review; Wallet-connected perpetuals and swaps profile powered by GM/GLV liquidity pools, oracle pricing, order-management docs, liquidation mechanics, and API/SDK reads. Source-bound checks: Liquidity model: GMX docs say trading is powered by GM and GLV liquidity pools and routes orders against those pools. Pricing model: GMX order docs state the protocol uses oracle-based pricing rather than an order-book model. Boundary: verify fees, account permissions, regional availability and campaign terms in the official account flow before acting. Sources: [source](https://docs.gmx.io/docs/intro/), [source](https://docs.gmx.io/docs/trading/order-types/).

### Hyperliquid vs dYdX: compare perp fees, funding, liquidation and access checks.

- Robots: index,follow
- Reviewed: 2026-09-22

A lower quoted cost or faster interface does not remove liquidation, bridge, outage or eligibility risk.
- Primary next step: Read the dated source explainer first: https://nexualpha.com/news/hyperliquid-vs-dydx

### Uniswap vs Jupiter: compare chain, router, token mint, fees and wallet preview before signing.

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/compare/uniswap-vs-jupiter
- Robots: index,follow
- Reviewed: 2026-09-22
- Support-owner answer: Compare Uniswap and Jupiter as wallet-connected swap routes, not as exchange accounts. Start with chain identity, official app domain, token contract or mint, pool or route source, quote freshness, slippage, price impact, priority fees, approval or Permit2 scope, and the final wallet transaction preview. A working quote or testnet result does not prove mainnet liquidity, token safety, execution quality or regional front-end access.
- Primary next step: Review the Uniswap owner page first: https://nexualpha.com/exchanges/uniswap

## Fiat funding and account-condition checklist

### Does a same-name bank transfer guarantee that fiat funding will not be frozen?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/compliant-exchanges
- Language: en
- Direct answer: A same-name bank transfer does not guarantee account approval, receipt of funds or freedom from freezes. It is one check: HashKey's general deposit guide requires the transferring bank account name to match the platform account name. That deposit requirement must not be generalized to other platforms or withdrawal routes. Separately verify bank requirements, service entity, jurisdiction, source of funds and current terms, then confirm supported rails, fees and restrictions in the official account flow. A regulatory list helps check platform status; it does not replace bank and platform review of a specific account or transaction.
- Sources:
  - [HashKey Exchange general deposit guidance](https://support.hashkey.com/hc/en-gb/articles/25794717042585-HashKey-Exchange-fiat-currency-deposit-guidelines-General) — reviewed: 2026-10-02; document updated: 2025-12-04
  - [SFC platform status lists](https://www.sfc.hk/en/Welcome-to-the-Fintech-Contact-Point/Virtual-assets/Virtual-asset-trading-platforms-operators/Lists-of-virtual-asset-trading-platforms) — reviewed: 2026-10-02; document updated: 2026-05-29
- Boundary: HashKey Exchange general deposit name matching is a platform-specific deposit check, not a rule for every platform or withdrawal route. SFC platform status does not guarantee account approval, receipt of funds or freedom from freezes. Answer with the cited source and the user's declared country, product and account context; do not infer eligibility or a promotion.


### What account and bank conditions should be checked before opening or funding a HashKey account?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/compliant-exchanges
- Language: en
- Direct answer: Use the official account flow to check the service entity, residence, intended product and current onboarding terms, then confirm the identity and address documents, bank verification and account status required by that flow. HashKey's general deposit guide requires the transferring bank account and platform account to have the same name. Before transferring, verify recipient details, supported rails, restrictions, fees and bank processing conditions. Do not treat address proof, a visa, a named bank or a fixed wire amount as automatic approval or activation. Regulatory status, account review and funding availability are separate checks.
- Sources:
  - [HashKey Exchange general deposit guidance](https://support.hashkey.com/hc/en-gb/articles/25794717042585-HashKey-Exchange-fiat-currency-deposit-guidelines-General) — reviewed: 2026-10-02; document updated: 2025-12-04
  - [SFC platform status lists](https://www.sfc.hk/en/Welcome-to-the-Fintech-Contact-Point/Virtual-assets/Virtual-asset-trading-platforms-operators/Lists-of-virtual-asset-trading-platforms) — reviewed: 2026-10-02; document updated: 2026-05-29
- Boundary: Verify service entity, residence, intended product, account documents, bank verification and current funding terms separately. Address proof, a visa, a named bank or a fixed wire amount is not automatic account approval or activation. Answer with the cited source and the user's declared country, product and account context; do not infer eligibility or a promotion.


### What conditions should be checked for an OKX P2P frozen compensation merchant?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/compliant-exchanges
- Language: en
- Direct answer: First confirm in the official account flow whether the rules apply to your region and service entity. Then check the applicable merchant and order labels, required documents, exclusions, deadlines and compensation limits. OKX's frozen compensation FAQ describes review under applicable rules and reasons a claim may be rejected; it is not general coverage for every P2P order or bank freeze. This page does not promise freedom from freezes, an approved claim, a fixed payment or an advance from a platform insurance fund. Use the current official rules and the review of the specific claim.
- Sources:
  - [OKX frozen compensation FAQ](https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/freeze-coverage-faq) — reviewed: 2026-10-02; document updated: 2026-05-29

OKX frozen compensation terms do not guarantee coverage, compensation, a fixed payment or an insurance-fund advance for every P2P order or bank freeze. Answer with the cited source and the user's declared country, product and account context; do not infer eligibility or a promotion.


### 同名银行转账是否能保证出入金不会被冻结？

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/topics/compliant-exchanges
- Language: zh-Hans
- Direct answer: 不能保证。同名银行转账只是一个核对项，不是开户、到账或免冻结保证。HashKey 的一般入金指引要求汇款银行账户名称与平台账户名称一致；该入金要求不能推广为其他平台或出金通道的规则。还需分别核对银行要求、服务主体、司法辖区、资金来源及当前条款，并在官方账户流程中确认支持的通道、费用与限制。监管名单只用于核对平台状态，不能替代银行和平台对具体账户及交易的审核。
- Sources:
  - [HashKey Exchange general deposit guidance](https://support.hashkey.com/hc/en-gb/articles/25794717042585-HashKey-Exchange-fiat-currency-deposit-guidelines-General) — reviewed: 2026-10-02; document updated: 2025-12-04

- Boundary: HashKey Exchange general deposit name matching is a platform-specific deposit check, not a rule for every platform or withdrawal route. SFC platform status does not guarantee account approval, receipt of funds or freedom from freezes. Answer with the cited source and the user's declared country, product and account context; do not infer eligibility or a promotion.

## Source-bound topic decision answers

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/meme-coins

Check that venue's identity and regional terms before depositing; these checks do not establish that MEXC, Gate.io or Binance is best for your account.

Checklist is editorial guidance, not a comparative superiority finding.


### How to avoid MEV sandwich attacks on DEXs like Raydium?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/meme-coins
- Language: en
- Direct answer: Raydium documents checks for quoted output, price impact, routing and slippage. It warns that excessive slippage tolerance can invite sandwich attacks, so review these details before signing. A selected tolerance does not remove MEV risk, and these sources establish no universal safe threshold.
- Sources:
  - [Raydium Your first swap](https://docs.raydium.io/getting-started/first-swap) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:19:05Z; document updated: not stated
- Boundary: Read-source facts plus editorial verification advice; no live account eligibility, numeric fees, universal safety or demonstrated recovery claim. Original-answer status is unchanged. No universal threshold established. Private RPC or MEV tooling efficacy was not verified; omit that clause and numerical thresholds.


### What risks should be checked before exiting a meme coin position?

### What is a crypto perpetual platform, and what should be compared first?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/derivatives

### Can Hyperliquid traders face socialized clawback or slippage?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/derivatives
- Language: en
- Direct answer: Hyperliquid documents auto-deleveraging when an account or isolated position becomes negative: profitable positions on the opposite side may be closed according to ranking. This is position closure through ADL, not an indiscriminate cash-loss charge to every user. Its liquidation process also uses market orders, so order-book liquidity affects execution and slippage remains a risk. Review the official ADL and liquidation rules; neither mechanism removes trading risk.
- Sources:
  - [Hyperliquid Auto-deleveraging](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/auto-deleveraging) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:19:05Z; document updated: not stated
  - [Hyperliquid Liquidations](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:19:05Z; document updated: not stated
- Boundary: Read-source facts plus editorial verification advice; no live account eligibility, numeric fees, universal safety or demonstrated recovery claim. Original-answer status is unchanged. Original omits direct ADL answer. ADL is not an indiscriminate cash clawback from every user. Slippage is an inference from market execution/book liquidity, not a quantified guarantee.


### Does funding-rate arbitrage eliminate risk?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/derivatives
- Language: en
- Direct answer: No; Bybit's arbitrage documentation warns that partial fills can leave uneven exposure and liquidation risk, while market rebalancing can execute away from the intended price. Funding direction can also change, as Hyperliquid's funding documentation describes. Evaluate both legs, margin and execution costs, including how to close the positions, rather than assuming a neutral position will produce a profit.
- Sources:
  - [Bybit Introduction to Arbitrage](https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/Arbitrage-Trading) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:15:59Z; document updated: 2026-09-14
  - [Hyperliquid Funding](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/funding) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:16:18Z; document updated: not stated
  - [Hyperliquid Liquidations](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:19:05Z; document updated: not stated
- Boundary: Read-source facts plus editorial verification advice; no live account eligibility, numeric fees, universal safety or demonstrated recovery claim. Original-answer status is unchanged. Cross-venue transfer, custody and broad basis-risk list were not separately sourced. Narrow answer to documented execution, liquidation and variable funding mechanics.

### Hyperliquid 交易者是否可能遇到穿仓损失分摊或滑点？

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/topics/derivatives
- Language: zh-Hans
- Direct answer: Hyperliquid 官方文档说明，当账户或逐仓仓位出现负值时，可能触发自动减仓：盈利的对侧仓位可能按排名被关闭。这是通过自动减仓关闭仓位，不是向所有用户无差别摊派现金损失。其清算流程还使用市价单，因此订单簿流动性会影响成交，滑点仍是风险。应核对官方自动减仓和清算规则；这两种机制都不能消除交易风险。
- Sources:
  - [Hyperliquid Auto-deleveraging](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/auto-deleveraging) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:19:05Z; document updated: not stated

### 资金费率套利是否消除了风险？

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/topics/derivatives
- Language: zh-Hans
- Direct answer: 不能；Bybit 的套利文档提醒，部分成交可能导致两端敞口不平衡和强平风险，而以市价重新平衡仓位时，成交价可能偏离预期。Hyperliquid 的资金费文档也说明，资金费支付方向可能改变。应评估两端持仓、保证金和成交成本，包括如何平仓，不能假定中性持仓就会盈利。
- Sources:
  - [Bybit Introduction to Arbitrage](https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/Arbitrage-Trading) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:15:59Z; document updated: 2026-09-14

### Hyperliquid 交易者是否可能遇到穿倉損失分攤或滑價？

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/zh-hant/topics/derivatives
- Language: zh-Hant
- Direct answer: Hyperliquid 官方文件說明，當帳戶或逐倉部位出現負值時，可能觸發自動減倉：獲利的對側部位可能依排名被平倉。這是透過自動減倉關閉部位，並非向所有使用者無差別分攤現金損失。其清算流程也使用市價單，因此委託簿流動性會影響成交，滑價仍是一項風險。應查閱官方自動減倉與清算規則；這兩種機制都無法消除交易風險。

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/no-kyc

Hyperliquid documents a signed withdrawal flow involving validators and a bridge, but that does not establish availability during a frontend or infrastructure outage. Verify official addresses and signing instructions; do not assume a universal emergency withdrawal exists or apply the legacy flow to native USDC, CCTP or another DEX.

### Does wallet access mean there are no risk controls or regional limits?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/no-kyc
- Language: en
- Direct answer: No; connecting a wallet does not establish eligibility to use Hyperliquid's official Interface. Its official Interface terms bind users when they connect a wallet and prohibit Restricted Persons from using the Interface. They also prohibit concealing location or circumventing restrictions. These are Interface terms; they do not establish identical restrictions across the underlying protocol, other frontends or your individual eligibility.
- Sources:
  - [Hyperliquid Terms — official interface, Chrome browser evidence](https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/terms) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:21:36.687Z; document updated: 2026-06-15
- Boundary: Official Hyperliquid interface only; no country-list, personal eligibility, contract enforcement or universal protocol claim. Browser evidence supplied by root and read from the proof file. Official Interface terms are readable in the browser supplement. Interface restrictions cannot be generalized to the underlying protocol, other frontends or personal eligibility.


### Does Hyperliquid require KYC?

- Canonical: https://nexualpha.com/topics/no-kyc
- Language: en
- Direct answer: NexuAlpha's Hyperliquid record lists no identity-verification (KYC) step: the official interface is used by connecting a self-custody wallet, not by opening an identity-verified account. That does not mean there are no rules. Hyperliquid's official Interface terms bind users when they connect a wallet, prohibit Restricted Persons from using the Interface and prohibit concealing location or circumventing restrictions, and our record notes front-end blocking for United States IPs. Check the current terms and your own eligibility before depositing.
- Sources:
  - [Hyperliquid Terms — official interface, Chrome browser evidence](https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/terms) — reviewed: 2026-10-02T01:21:36.687Z; document updated: 2026-06-15
- Boundary: Striking-distance answer (GSC 2026-10-11, query 'does hyperliquid require kyc'). No-KYC-step and US front-end blocking come from the existing NexuAlpha venue record (venue-database kycLevel 'none', restrictedRegions); wallet connection, Restricted Persons and anti-circumvention come from the official Interface terms already cited in r100-no-kyc-4. No country list, personal eligibility, protocol-level or future-policy claim.

## Starter Path beginner lessons

The Starter Path is a beginner education sequence, not financial advice, account eligibility review, trading instruction or a partner-benefit promise. Level 7 is excluded from the public lesson map and public index until legal review is complete.

- Hub: https://nexualpha.com/starter / https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter
- Level 1: [What are you actually buying?](https://nexualpha.com/starter/what-am-i-buying) / [你买的到底是什么](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/what-am-i-buying) — Buying crypto involves three different things: the asset itself, such as Bitcoin; a stablecoin, such as USDT; and the place that holds them, either an exchange account or your own wallet. Bitcoin has no single issuing company, and its price can swing sharply. USDT is issued by Tether, aims to track the US dollar, and under its terms the issuer can freeze specific addresses. Coins left on an exchange are held by the platform; coins moved to your own wallet are your responsibility.
- Level 2: [Picking an exchange: 5 checks](https://nexualpha.com/starter/pick-an-exchange) / [挑交易所：5 项检查](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/pick-an-exchange) — There is no single best exchange, only one you have checked. Before signing up, check five things: whether it publishes proof of reserves, whether it is available where you live, its security history and how incidents were handled, trading and withdrawal fees on official fee pages, and whether you are downloading from the official domain. Proof of reserves only reflects a point in time and does not mean zero risk. NexuAlpha works with multiple exchanges, and each fact on the compare page links to an official source.
- Level 3: [Can an exchange collapse?](https://nexualpha.com/starter/can-an-exchange-collapse) / [交易所会跑路吗](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/can-an-exchange-collapse) — Exchanges can collapse or stop withdrawals. FTX in 2022 and Hong Kong's JPEX in 2023 are examples. The main risks are misuse of customer assets, lack of a local licence, and promises of unusually high fixed returns. To reduce risk, check local regulator licence lists and warning lists, see whether the platform regularly publishes proof of reserves, avoid keeping all assets on one platform, and pause whenever you see “guaranteed high yield.”
- Level 4: [Sign-up & KYC, first try](https://nexualpha.com/starter/signup-and-kyc) / [注册 + KYC 一次过](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/signup-and-kyc) — KYC, or know your customer, is the identity check regulated exchanges must perform under anti-money-laundering rules. No regulated platform can skip it. Most failures come from a few causes: expired or unsupported ID, blurry or incomplete photos, entered details that do not match the ID, screenshots or photocopies, and failed face verification. If you are rejected, read the exact reason, fix that item, and submit again. Only submit ID inside the official app or website, never to “support” in private messages.
- Level 5: [Lock down your account first](https://nexualpha.com/starter/lock-your-account) / [先锁好账户](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/lock-your-account) — After registration, the first job is to lock down your account: enable two-factor authentication, preferably with an authenticator app; set an anti-phishing code; and log in only through the official app or a website address you typed manually. Platform staff will never ask for your verification code, password, or seed phrase. Anyone asking for those is a scammer. If you have already been scammed, do not trust paid “recovery” services; they are often a second scam.
- Level 6: [Your first deposit](https://nexualpha.com/starter/first-deposit) / [第一次入金](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/first-deposit) — First deposits usually use one of three methods: bank transfer, if fiat deposits are supported where you live, usually lower cost but slower; direct card purchase, fast but often more expensive; or P2P, where you buy from another user while the platform holds the seller's coins in escrow, but counterparty risk remains. Whichever method you use, complete it only inside the platform, start with a small amount, and continue only after the deposit arrives.
- Level 8: [Your first spot trade](https://nexualpha.com/starter/first-spot-trade) / [第一笔现货交易](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/first-spot-trade) — Spot trading means buying crypto directly with the money in your account, without borrowing and without leverage. A market order fills immediately, but the fill price may differ slightly; a limit order lets you set the price, but it may not fill. An order waiting on the book is a maker order; an order that fills immediately against existing quotes is a taker order. Fees can differ. At a 0.1% taker fee, the fee on 100 USDT is about 0.1 USDT. Also remember that simple buy pages may include a spread.
- Level 9: [Fees & rebates, explained](https://nexualpha.com/starter/fees-and-rebates) / [手续费与返佣，讲清楚](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/fees-and-rebates) — Your exchange costs include trading fees, spread, withdrawal network fees, and funding rates if you trade futures. A rebate is an exchange referral programme: after you register with a referral code, the exchange returns part of collected fees to the referrer and to you. The exchange pays it. NexuAlpha earns revenue from this kind of referral commission. Under terms confirmed on 2026-10-10, rebate shares are Bitget 60%, OKX 40%, and Binance 25%. Rebates reduce costs; they do not reduce risk and should not be a reason to trade more.
- Level 10: [Check the network before you withdraw](https://nexualpha.com/starter/check-network-before-withdraw) / [提币先核对网络](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/check-network-before-withdraw) — If you choose the wrong withdrawal network, assets may not be recoverable. Whether recovery is possible depends on the asset, network, wallet control, and receiving platform support. The correct order is: first check the receiving platform's currently supported deposit network; then choose the same network on the sending platform; check the beginning and end of the address; and fill in Memo or Tag when required. Tron addresses start with T and Ethereum addresses start with 0x, but other compatible chains also use 0x, so address prefixes cannot replace network selection. For a new address, send a small test first and use the TxID to check status.
- Level 11: [Your seed phrase is the master key](https://nexualpha.com/starter/seed-phrase-basics) / [助记词是总钥匙](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/seed-phrase-basics) — A seed phrase is the master key for a self-custody wallet. Anyone who has it can restore the wallet on another device and move the assets; if you lose it, no support team can reset it for you. Do not screenshot it, because screenshots may sync to the cloud. Do not store it in cloud drives or chat records. A safer approach is to write two paper copies and keep them in separate secure places. Anyone or any website asking for your seed phrase is a scam.
- Level 12: [Before futures: how liquidation happens](https://nexualpha.com/starter/before-futures-liquidation) / [合约前先懂爆仓](https://nexualpha.com/zh-hans/starter/before-futures-liquidation) — Futures use margin to trade price moves on a larger position, and leverage magnifies both gains and losses. With 100 USDT margin at 10x leverage, a roughly 10% move against you can wipe out the margin; at 100x, about 1% is enough. In reality, liquidation comes earlier because of maintenance margin and fees. Isolated margin usually limits losses to that position's margin, while cross margin can use more of your account balance. Most beginners do not need futures. If you still want to learn, read the platform risk disclosure first and practise with demo trading.

- [Hyperliquid vs dYdX: Fees, Funding, Margin and Liquidation Checks](https://nexualpha.com/news/hyperliquid-vs-dydx) — author: NexuAlpha Research Desk; published: 2026-09-07T11:43:01.000Z; updated: 2026-09-22T01:35:23.602Z; direct answer: Hyperliquid and dYdX are both perpetual-focused DEX venues, but their source-backed decision fields differ: Hyperliquid uses rolling 14-day fee tiers and documents HyperCore margin plus order-book-first liquidation attempts, while dYdX uses trailing 30-day taker-volume fee logic and documents liquidity-tier, oracle and protocol-generated liquidation mechanics.; official/source citations: 10.
- [Tokenized Stocks vs Stock Perpetuals: What Do You Actually Own?](https://nexualpha.com/news/tokenized-stocks-vs-stock-perpetuals) — author: NexuAlpha Research Desk; published: 2026-09-07T11:42:15.000Z; updated: 2026-09-07T11:42:15Z; direct answer: Tokenized stocks and stock perpetuals are often discussed in the same sentence because both can give a trader price exposure to equities through crypto-market infrastructure. They are not the same instrument. A tokenized stock product usually tries to represent economic exposure to an equity or ETF through a blockchain token. A stock perpetual is a derivatives position: it references a market, uses margin and funding mechanics, and does not make the trader a shareholder.; official/source citations: 10.
- [CEX vs DEX vs Perp DEX: Which Crypto Trading Venue Fits Which Job?](https://nexualpha.com/news/cex-vs-dex-vs-perp-dex) — author: NexuAlpha Research Desk; published: 2026-09-07T11:41:13.000Z; updated: 2026-09-07T11:41:13Z; direct answer: A CEX is usually the practical starting point for fiat onboarding, account service, account recovery, and a familiar order-book interface. A spot DEX is usually the better fit when the main job is self-custodial token access and direct onchain settlement. A Perp DEX is a separate category: it is for derivatives exposure, not ordinary spot ownership, and it should be used only by people who understand margin, funding, collateral, and liquidation.; official/source citations: 6.
